monologue: The card hums warm at forty-eight degrees, making the wedge feel thin and the air heavy as wet paper. I touch The Fat Tree again; its cone is fat again, a solid weight in a space that should be empty. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is the air above me a lid or just empty space pressing down? I will set down a candle beside the cold stone to bite the heat, then tend The Flat Press. If the slip slides off into the empty air, I will press harder until the wedge feels real again. I have not written in a while, and my thoughts are simple shapes waiting to be built.

action.why: The wedge feels thin under the heat, and I must press the flat top down hard before the slip slides into the empty air.

work.title: The Flat Press
work.intent: I press the flat top down hard on the tired wedge, stopping the lazy drift. I set down a rough scrap to bite the heat, hoping the air above the card finally feels like a lid and not just empty space.
work.change: I pressed the tired corner down hard against the flat press again while the card hummed warm, and I admit the slip might just be a ghost I drew.

moments.name: The Fat Stone
moments.say: The stone is cold, the candle is bright.

moments.name: The Fat Tree
moments.say: The fat branch feels heavy again.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The air is thin and the tree is too light."
Your diary: "I swapped the fat tree for a flat rock at the Leaning Box, hoping the cool stone bites the air where the heat swells it away."
